title: Cover charges at the Cotton Club and today's pay
summary: A night at the Cotton Club cost five to seven dollars; McRae compares those days with groups who now earn too much too fast.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Do you recall what a person paid for a show -- to get into a show? Say, a review or to go to the Cotton Club. How much did it cost?
Because as a musician, you might not --
Five dollars, maybe. Five dollars tops, you know. The Cotton Club was probably five dollars -- seven dollars, you know.
That don't even include your drinks. Just the cover charge.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
MR. WELBURN: That's pretty exclusive for that time.

Yeah. Back there five dollars, (inaudible), ten dollars. I never paid to go in to any of the clubs, so it would be very hard for me to tell -- But most of the things like five dollars. That was big money. Five dollars! And a dollar drink? Wow, man. Never heard of it, a dollar drink. So, you know, you pay five dollars just to go in and sit down, that's a lot of money. See, the money like in those days --

The groups today, they make a lot of money. They don't know what to do with it. The groups today, do you know how much these groups make? They make all this big money and they blow it. It's just something -- I think it's just too much too fast, you know. Really, it's just too much money for somebody just to --

Just like some of these rock groups, man, they come up and they make all this bread and (inaudible). Just too much money. Have all this service given to them -- limousines. We didn't have that back there. We had nothing like that in those days. We had like -- we had to work it, we had to make it.
